particularites.text: Loss of exclusivity for BRIVIACT (antiepileptic) in Europe from August 2026, with an expected decline of roughly 80% in US sales over the following 12 months - headwind already identified by management for H2 26, distinct from the momentum of the 5 growth drivers (BIMZELX first among them).

Acquisitions of Neurona Therapeutics (cell therapy, epilepsy) and Candid Therapeutics in H1 26, partly debt-financed: the net position moved from net cash of 7 M€ at end-2025 to net debt of 2 821 M€ at end-June 2026 (with the dividend paid and buybacks over the same period) - temporary deterioration of the balance sheet, without calling into question the deleveraging trajectory given the group's growing cash generation.

ownership.insiderDesc: Financiere de Tubize SA (family control vehicle created in 1928, bringing together the descendants of founder Emmanuel Janssen and the shareholders who share their long-term vision) holds around 36% of the capital - explicitly stated objective of shareholder stability and family predominance for UCB's long-term industrial development.
ownership.insiderSource: Financiere de Tubize corporate communications (2025-2026) cross-checked with UCB's publications.
ownership.coverageNote: No tier-1 watchlist investor identified with a notable position - broad and passive institutional shareholder base (FMR/Fidelity ~7%, BlackRock ~6%, Vanguard ~2,8%), with no named conviction manager beyond the family control block via Financiere de Tubize.

items.title: Allegation of illegal kickbacks to physicians prescribing Cimzia (via free education/reimbursement services), brought by a relator (CIMZNHCA LLC) under the US False Claims Act.
items.outcome: The US government declined to intervene and moved to dismiss the action, stating after investigation that the allegations were unfounded; dismissal upheld by the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals (2020).
items.source: United States ex rel. CIMZNHCA, LLC v. UCB, Inc., 970 F.3d 835 (7th Cir. 2020)

compliance.note: A single item identified across the public history searched (2020 allegation, dropped by the US courts). Patent litigation identified elsewhere (Cimzia vs Kennedy Institute Trust, Yeda Research - the latter decided in UCB's favour) excluded from the scope as it falls under ordinary commercial/patent litigation, not a fraud allegation.

clesRetenues: Q Peter Verdult (BNP Paribas) - Phase III data for Galvokimig in atopic dermatitis and comfort with the BIMZELX 2026 consensus: data readout expected in early 2028 (enrolment accelerating); management confirms its comfort with the Visible Alpha 2026 consensus; BE BOLD data (June EULAR) showing superiority over SKYRIZI, first physician reactions very positive.

Q Sarita Kapila (Morgan Stanley) - emerging competition in hidradenitis suppurativa (Novartis' oral remibrutinib, AbbVie's lutikizumab): CMO Emmanuel Caeymaex regards BIMZELX's dual IL-17A/F blockade as central in HS, no competitor data suggest superior efficacy, the heterogeneity of HS patients justifies a plurality of approaches.

Q Sophia Graeff Buhl-Nielsen (JPMorgan) - BIMZELX distribution channel mix and penetration of the government channel: the company does not disclose the channel mix in detail, continued progress in the commercial and government segments; too early to identify predictive markers of response to anti-IL-17 treatment.

Q Xian Deng (UBS) - detail of the first-line access agreement with a large PBM and breakdown of the 7 Md€ peak sales target for BIMZELX: agreement effective 1 June covering the three indications in first line with that PBM; peak sales breakdown by indication not disclosed, reflects different stages of competition/penetration.

Q Charles Pitman-King (Barclays) - quantification of the pressure on BIMZELX's net price and sustainability of the R&D ratio: CFO Sandrine Dufour gives no precise quantified trend on net price (mix of double step-edit / single step-edit / first line); medium-term R&D target around 25% of net sales, 2027 guidance judged premature at this stage.

Q Charlie Haywood (Bank of America) - mechanics of the EBITDA margin decline in H2 vs H1: H2 headwinds identified - BRIVIACT loss of exclusivity (Europe in August, US decline expected at 80% over 12 months), lower gross-to-net benefits, erosion of BIMZELX's access price ahead of the volume ramp, heavier R&D phasing in H2, acquisition integration costs.

Q Kerry Holford (Berenberg) - long-term margin guidance and appetite for business development: no long-term margin guidance given, objective of gradual improvement; myasthenia gravis (gMG) franchise growing 38% year on year thanks to the FcRn/C5 dual therapy; BD focus on early-stage assets, integration capacity managed through 2035 and beyond.

Q Rudy Li (Wolfe Research) - key drivers of the 7 Md€ target for BIMZELX: field execution/channel optimisation, clinical data (BE BOLD published in June 2026), lifecycle extension (PPP trial, adolescent indications).

Q Michael Leuchten (Jefferies) - effectiveness of the BIMZELX DTC campaign (NBRx trends) and capital allocation to bepranemab (anti-tau antibody) after the Biogen data at AAIC: sustained DTC investment, the November quiet period explains a one-off dip in new prescriptions, back to full speed since; Biogen data judged supportive of the extracellular tau hypothesis, regulatory alignment finalised over the last 6 months for a confirmatory Phase II study.

Quantified context for the year: net sales +35% at constant currency to 7,4 Md€, adjusted EBITDA +79% to 2,6 Md€ (margin 34%, +10pt), core EPS doubled to 9,99€; BIMZELX more than tripled to over 2,2 Md€, leader of the IL-17 class in the United States (>30% share in psoriasis, 45% in HS).
Initial 2026 guidance communicated: high-single-digit/low-double-digit sales growth (subsequently revised up in H1 26 towards 'low-teens to mid-teens').
Q (plans for bepranemab in Alzheimer's) - CEO Jean-Christophe Tellier acknowledges the risks inherent in Alzheimer's programmes and indicates that UCB remains open to partnerships to share that risk.

engagementsStructurants.engagement: Phase III data readout for Galvokimig (atopic dermatitis) expected in early 2028, enrolment accelerating according to management.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No standalone H2 guidance (UCB guides on the full year only), but the CFO walked through the H2-vs-H1 mechanics: BRIVIACT loss of exclusivity weighted to H2, no repeat of the ~EUR 100m prior-year gross-to-net benefit, BIMZELX net-price erosion from the June 1 first-line PBM agreement before volumes build, and heavier R&D phasing (new studies plus Neurona/Candid integration) - so the H2 EBITDA margin steps down from H1's 40.7%.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 guidance raised (upgrade vs the initial February frame): net sales growth low-teens to mid-teens at constant rates (initially high-single-digit to low-double-digit), adjusted EBITDA growth mid-teens to low-20s at constant rates, core tax rate ~15%; full-year R&D ratio near 25% of net sales and full-year gross margin still expected up vs 2025 (product mix more than offsetting net-price effects); guidance excludes any potential US most-favored-nation pricing or tariff impact.
pointsCles: H1 26 net sales +23% (+28% CER) to EUR 4.09bn and adjusted EBITDA +68% (+79% CER) to EUR 1.74bn (40.7% margin, explicitly flagged as phasing-inflated); core EPS EUR 6.84 vs 3.53 a year ago, far above the EUR 5.03 consensus, with IFRS net income of EUR 1,111m (basic EPS 5.83).

BIMZELX doubled YoY to EUR 1.5bn and peak-sales target raised to at least EUR 7bn (IL-17 dynamic shares ~35% psoriasis, ~30% rheumatology, ~45% HS; >135,000 patients, >50 countries); first-line access across all three indications at a major US PBM effective June 1, on top of 80% commercial covered lives and the BE BOLD superiority readout vs SKYRIZI (ACR50) published at EULAR in June.

H2 26 headwinds spelled out by the CFO: BRIVIACT LOE weighted to H2 (US generics since February, ~80% 12-month US decline; Europe LOE in August, ~-50%), non-recurrence of the ~EUR 100m prior-year gross-to-net benefit, BIMZELX net-price erosion ahead of the first-line volume build, and heavier H2 R&D phasing plus Neurona/Candid integration costs.

Five growth drivers now deliver >50% of group net sales (gMG portfolio +38% to EUR 330m, EVENITY net contribution +34% to EUR 379m, FINTEPLA +18% to EUR 239m); pipeline advanced on all fronts - bepranemab into confirmatory Phase II, galvokimig AD readout targeted early 2028 plus COPD/bronchiectasis expansion, rezanecel (Neurona) Phase III in H1 27, cizutamig (Candid) Phase II in gMG and SARD-ILD.

hypothese.summary: Belgian biopharma under stable family control (Financiere de Tubize, ~36%), accelerating sharply on the back of BIMZELX (peak sales target raised to at least 7 Md€) and 4 other growth drivers; H2 26 has to absorb several identified headwinds (BRIVIACT loss of exclusivity, pressure on BIMZELX's net price) before the ramp-up continues in 2027.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Century-old family-controlled Belgian biopharma (Tubize ~36%) in neurology/immunology, past its 2021-2023 LOE trough and accelerating on BIMZELX (anti-IL-17A/F): sales tripled in 2025 to >2.2bn, doubled again in H1 26 to 1.5bn, peak-sales target raised to >=7bn with class-leading US IL-17 share. FY26 guided: net sales low-to-mid-teens cc, adjusted EBITDA mid-teens-to-low-20s cc, core tax ~15%.

== THESIS READ ==
- BIMZELX is executing at or above the raised curve - the single dominant thesis driver. Watch: US HS/PsA prescription trends and EU pricing.
- Operating leverage phase: EBITDA guided to grow faster than sales - margin expansion is the second engine. Watch: SG&A discipline as launches scale.
- Pipeline behind BIMZELX (galvokimig, dovistamab, epilepsy franchise durability) remains lightly valued. Watch: 2026-2027 readouts.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Semi-annual reporter (H1 + February FY) - quarterly structures use H1/H2 labels. Basis wedge documented: projections track CORE net (consensus metric) vs IFRS 'data'; the bridge 'other' line carries the core add-backs explicitly. Historical shares/net debt 2021-2024 estimated by cross-check (flagged); 'ebit' series from an aggregated source, to verify against the annual report. priorEPS null (young fiche).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: sales 8,825M (+14% cc mid), core net 2,208M / core EPS 11.62 (consensus-aligned); 2027-2030: ~+12%/yr sales fading, margin expansion, net cash from 2029. Core tax ~15% guided. Watch: verify ebit series; Feb FY26 initial-guidance backfill for the anchor; Vimpat/Keppra generic tails.

== CATALYSTS ==
FY26 results (Feb 2027) with FY27 guidance; BIMZELX quarterly trajectory via US scripts; pipeline readouts; possible index-inclusion flows.

ancrages.moteur: BIMZELX in confirmed hypergrowth: sales more than tripled in 2025 (>2,2 Md€), doubled again in H1 26 (1,5 Md€), peak sales target raised to at least 7 Md€ supported by a first-line access agreement with a large US PBM (effective June 2026) and clinical superiority data (BE BOLD study).

BRIVIACT loss of exclusivity identified as an H2 26 headwind (Europe from August, US decline ~80% over 12 months) - transitory revenue-mix effect, distinct from the structural momentum of the 5 growth drivers.

Operating jaws effect confirmed: adjusted EBITDA margin up from 24% (2024) to 34% (2025), 2026 guidance for EBITDA growth above sales growth ('mid-teens to low-20s' vs 'low-teens to mid-teens') - margin expansion expected to continue as the growth drivers scale up.

Neurona Therapeutics and Candid Therapeutics acquisitions (H1 26) taking net debt to 2,8 Md€ at end-June 2026 (against near-zero net cash at end-2025); deleveraging expected to be driven by the group's growing cash generation (EBITDA/sales jaws effect), with management saying it is 'reasonably equipped through 2035+' to absorb additional business development targeted at early-stage assets.

Stable family control via Financiere de Tubize (~36% of the capital) since 1928, governance geared to stability and long-term industrial development - consistent with the targeted business development strategy (early-stage assets rather than opportunistic large-scale M&A).
